entry.title: Characterize Nanoparticles - Malvern Panalytical Zetasizer Ultra at the VINSE Analytical Laboratory

media:group.media:title: Characterize Nanoparticles - Malvern Panalytical Zetasizer Ultra at the VINSE Analytical Laboratory
media:group.media:description:
The Malvern Panalytical Zetasizer Ultra at the Vanderbilt Institute of Nanoscale Science and Engineering (VINSE) provides rapid, high-precision measurements of particle and molecular size, zeta potential (surface charge), molecular weight and particle concentration to help solve complex formulation challenges.
Whether you're optimizing a new formulation, conducting advanced materials research or troubleshooting an unstable product, the Zetasizer Ultra delivers the data you need with confidence.
Learn how the instrument can: • Measure particle sizes from 0.3 nm to 10 µm • Determine zeta potential to assess colloidal stability • Analyze complex, multimodal particle distributions • Quantify particle concentration quickly and accurately
VINSE's Analytical Laboratory provides access to state-of-the-art characterization tools for academic and industrial users. Our staff can assist with sample analysis, training, and experimental design.
To learn more or request access, visit: https://www.vanderbilt.edu/vinse/

entry.title: Audio Storytelling and the Sound of Discovery with Jad Abumrad

media:group.media:title: Audio Storytelling and the Sound of Discovery with Jad Abumrad
media:group.media:description:
Jad Abumrad (https://as.vanderbilt.edu/communication-science-technology/bio/jad-abumrad/) , acclaimed journalist, podcast creator, Vanderbilt professor, and one of the most influential audio storytellers of our time, thought he was going to live his life as a musician. Like any good story, his life took an unexpected turn and he used his musical and composing skills to launch a new form of radio journalism, podcasting.
Abumrad, Distinguished Research Professor of Communication of Science and Technology, is the creator and longtime host of Radiolab, the groundbreaking podcast that transformed how millions of people engage with science, philosophy, and human experience through sound, as well as the beloved podcast series Dolly Parton’s America. This year, Abumrad became the first Vanderbilt faculty member to receive the prestigious Peabody Award for “the most powerful and enlightening stories in all of television, radio, and online media” for his podcast series Fela Kuti: Fear No Man, produced in Vanderbilt’s Studio 608 podcast studio.
In this episode of the Quantum Potential (https://www.vanderbilt.edu/research/) podcast, Abumrad sits on the other side of the microphone, as he talks about the art of audio storytelling, music, and the journey that brought him to where he is today.

entry.title: Chronic Pain Innovations Beyond Opioids with Lori Schirle

media:group.media:title: Chronic Pain Innovations Beyond Opioids with Lori Schirle
media:group.media:description:
Millions of people experience severe pain or know someone suffering with chronic pain. For decades, opioids have been the default treatment, especially after surgery. But reactions to opioids— and the relief or consequences that result— differ from person to person. On this episode of the Quantum Potential (https://www.vanderbilt.edu/research/) podcast, Lori Schirle (https://www.vumc.org/anesthesiology/person/lori-schirle-phd-crna) , assistant professor at the Vanderbilt University School of Nursing, certified registered nurse anesthetist and nurse scientist, explains her transformative research on understanding pain and relief alternatives.
Her research explores whether differences in our DNA can help predict who is most likely to experience persistent discomfort after surgery and who may not respond well to opioids.
She also explains innovations in personalized pain treatment research, supported by the National Institutes of Health and Vanderbilt’s Seeding Success Grant program (https://www.vanderbilt.edu/research-development-and-support/internal-funding-programs/seeding-success-grant/) , that takes an entirely new approach to easing pain by focusing on the brain.
